By this Appeal, the Appellant questioned the Judgment and order 2/5 60.Judg.fa.479.2017.odt dated 25/2/2015 passed by the Civil Judge Senior Division, Washim in Land Acquisition Case No.
94/2003.
In the present Appeal, admittedly, the land admeasuring 2 H. 84 R. out of Survey No. 186 of village Kinkheda Tahsil and District Washim was acquired by the Respondents for Karli Dam.
The Notification under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued on 23/9/1998.
As per the Award dated 30/9/2000, the Special Land Acquisition officer has awarded the compensation at the rate of Rs.16,500/- per hectare to the Appellant.

The Appellant, being aggrieved by the said Award,
preferred the reference proceeding for seeking enhancement of amount of compensation.

2. The Appellant, before the learned Reference Court, has relied upon the decision passed by the Reference Court in LAC No. 89/2003 dated 15/5/2009, whereby the enhancement was granted in the said matter at the rate of Rs.60,000/- per hectare.
It is also stated by the Appellant that if the enhancement is granted at the rate of Rs.60,000/- per hectare, the Appellant will waive the compensation towards the trees and damages in the matter.
Accordingly, the learned Reference Court, by relying upon the Judgment dated 15/5/2009 in LAC No. 89/2003, enhanced the compensation at the rate of Rs.60,000/- per hectare to the Appellant.
Being aggrieved by the said Judgment passed by the Reference Court, the Appellant has filed present Appeal and sought further enhancement in the compensation amount.

By this Appeal, the Appellant is claiming additional compensation of Rs.3,62,100/- along with interest and other components thereon, on the ground that land acquired was an irrigated land, but compensation is granted by treating the same as dry crop land.
4.

The learned Counsel appearing for the Respondent No.3 has placed reliance upon the Judgment of this Court in First Appeal No. 1087/2015 (Executive Engineer, Minor Irrigation Division, Washim V/s Bhaurao Ashruji Saoke & Ors.) dated 7/9/2021.

entities.text: First Appeal No. 1087/2015 (Executive Engineer, Minor Irrigation Division, Washim V/s Bhaurao Ashruji Saoke & Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court, while dealing with the issue of enhancement of compensation, has relied upon the Judgment in LAC No. 89/2003 and held that for dry crop land, the valuation at the rate of Rs.60,000/- per hectare.

Therefore, it is the submission of the Respondent No.3 that once this Court has upheld the Judgment passed in LAC No. 89/2003,
which is also relied by the learned Reference Court in the matter, there is no need of interference of this Court in the present matter.

5. In the present Appeal, it is admitted fact that the Appellant has admitted before the Reference Court that if the compensation is granted as per the Judgment in LAC No. 89/2003, he will be satisfied and even not claimed 4/5 60.Judg.fa.479.2017.odt any compensation towards the trees as well as damages.

For that purpose, the Appellant has also placed on record pursis (Exhibit-29)
before the Reference Court, meaning thereby that the Appellant was satisfied with the compensation of Rs.60,000/- per hectare awarded in the matter for dry crop land.
So also the same was confirmed by this Court in First Appeal No. 1087/2015.
6. The Appellant, to demonstrate the fact that land acquired was an irrigated land, has relied upon the 7/12 extract (Exhibit-21).

However, perusal of the same no where shows that land was an Narayan Sakharam Ghule vs The State Of Maharashtra, Thr. ... on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146119704/
2 irrigated land.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the contrary, perusal of the crops recorded on Exhibit-21 clearly shows that same are taken from dry crop land.
There is no mention of having any well in the field.
Hence, I am not satisfied on the submission of Appellant that land was an irrigated land.

7. The Respondent No.3 has pointed out from the cross-examination of Appellant that he admitted the fact that he failed to produce on record any evidence to show that acquired land was an irrigated land and there is no mention of having water-well in the field nor established that he was taking water from any other place.
8. As such, I am of the view that no interference of this Court is 5/5 60.Judg.fa.479.2017.odt warranted in the present matter.
The present Appeal is devoid of merits, hence, dismissed with no order as to costs.
